transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Evan, Priya, Miguel, Hannah, Lena, Mark, Tom

Summary:
Quick internal enablement session to iterate on short micro-pitches, rehearse 3-minute demos for common buyer profiles, and capture fresh competitive rebuttals. Focus on speed, repeatability, and clear handoffs for follow-up playbook updates.

Topics:
- 3 micro-pitch templates (PLG startup, mid-market product team, regulated enterprise)
- Rapid demo checklist (30s setup, 90s highlight, 60s close + next steps)
- Competitive one-liners and fallback play (Anthropic/OpenAI differentiation)
- Common objections: cost/latency, private deployment, SOC2/compliance, model quality regressions

Transcript body:
[00:00] Evan: Alright folks, kicking off, thanks for carving the hour fifteen, um, we wanted to try a slightly different format today — a hack-sprint, micro-pitches then live demo sprints. Keep it rough, the goal is repeatable 3 minute hits.

[00:23] Priya: Yeah hi everyone, I, I mapped out three buyer personas, quick note, these are intentionally templated so AEs can swap in specifics. I'll go first with the PLG startup pitch.

[00:37] Priya: So — hi I'm Priya from Redwood Inference — we help teams run LLM inference reliably without managing the full stack. Two things most PLG startups care about: fast time-to-value and predictable costs. So micropitch would be: "Ship features faster with a hosted API that scales, and when you need predictability, move to Dedicated GPU pools with simple billing and predictable throughput."

[01:02] Tom: Quick interruption, I like the move to mention Dedicated but maybe call out autoscaling/burst so they don't think it's all reserved capacity.

[01:10] Priya: Good call. I'll add "configurable autoscale with burst".

[01:16] Miguel: Also mention that the runtime has prefix caching — some folks hear caching and think it's complex, so say "automatic prefix/K-V cache that reduces token costs" — though note the transcriptist spelled it K-V or K-V cache sometimes.

[01:31] Lena: On the enterprise/regulatory side we need a quick line about Private: "VPC or on-prem options with KMS integrations and audit logs". That's the opener for heavily regulated buyers.

[01:44] Evan: Great. Let's go demo sprint format now — Miguel you'll do the mid-market demo, 3 minutes — timeboxing: 30s setup, 90s show-us, 60s close. I'll timebox and interrupt if you hit 2:45.

[01:58] Miguel: Cool. Starting setup: "This is Redwood Console, quick token-level breakdown on a per-route dashboard, you can see latency p95 and cost per route, and jump into traces."

[02:18] Miguel: Show: choose model from catalog — redwood verified profiles — spin up a test request on hosted API, show streaming output. Then flip to Dedicated config, show pool size and autoscaling policy and illustrate fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant when capacity is constrained.

[02:45] (minor crosstalk)

[03:00] Miguel: Close: "If you want to try this exact flow, we can run a 2-week pilot with Reserved capacity and daily syncs to tune batching and caching settings."

[03:10] Evan: Okay that was good — couple of quick notes: you said "quantized variant" — for sales decks sometimes 'quantized' confuses AEs; use 'lower-cost model variant' as default phrasing. Also be explicit about fallback — "automatic fallback to compatible model variants to avoid outages".

[03:33] Mark: On objections — when folks ask about latency vs cost, we should have a standard response: "We expose levers — batching, cache, and model selection — and we can simulate your traffic to show tradeoffs". Can we get a short sentence for decks?

[03:50] Hannah: I'll draft a one-liner: "We give you predictable levers to tune latency and cost — from batch sizing to KV caching to model quantization — and we run benchmarks on your traces so you know the impact in dollars per 1k tokens."

[04:10] Priya: Love it. Let's do the mock objection roleplay. Tom you're the buyer, ask the security Qs.

[04:20] Tom: Ok quick: "What about compliance? We have PCI and SOC2 requirements and can't send user PII to a third-party."

[04:30] Priya (as AE): "Totally. For regulated data we'd recommend Redwood Private — VPC/private control plane with optional on-prem, audit logs, and KMS/HSM integrations. We can also set data retention policies and sign an addendum for data handling."

[04:48] Tom: What's the timeline for a Private deployment?

[04:52] Priya: Typical on-prem proof-of-concept is 4–8 weeks depending on infra approvals; VPC deployment in a region can be weeks not months if there's an existing cloud account.

[05:05] (paper shuffling)

[05:12] Miguel: There's also the gating question of which stakeholders to include — infra, security, and the product owner. We should add that to the playbook checklist: 'Stakeholders: Infra, InfoSec, Product, APAC legal if relevant.'

[05:28] Evan: Yeah add that. Ok next micro-pitch — Tom do the enterprise one quickly.

[05:34] Tom: "We help enterprise teams standardize inference across hosted, dedicated, and private — same API, same tooling, rollouts and canary policies — so they don't rewrite integrations later."

[05:46] Lena: We should call out rollouts and automatic fallback more plainly: 'canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies keep production stable' — quick win line.

[05:58] Evan: Now let's spice up competitive angle. Miguel, on Anthropic/OpenAI questions — what's a tight two-sentence take?

[06:08] Miguel: "We focus on serving and production economics — many vendors focus on models only; Redwood focuses on predictable inference with ops tooling: token-level cost visibility, batching controls, and private deployment patterns. If the ask is model coverage, we have a model catalog and can route to different model variants."

[06:30] Hannah: Add a micro rebuttal: "If they say 'we already use X provider' — reply 'great, we can integrate and optimize around that stack, or if you need predictable SLAs and private deployment, our Dedicated and Private options are engineered for that.'"

[06:45] Mark: Also call out that we have quality monitoring e.g., eval regressions tied to prompt sets — that's a differential vs raw model APIs.

[06:55] Priya: Let's do a demo of a 'failure and fallover' quickly — I'll simulate a high load and show how routing sends requests to fallback model.

[07:05] (screen share noise)

[07:12] Priya: Alright on my screen — this is the routing policy page, show priority routing, set capacity threshold to 85% then simulate 120% load. Watch request stream — the runtime reroutes to a compatible lower-cost variant; logs show the fallback and trace IDs. Uh, the auto transcript spells trace as 'trays' sometimes.

[07:45] Evan: Nice — that visual is gold for the demo. For the one-pager cheat sheet, we should screenshot that and add a two-sentence caption: 'Automatic fallback reduces outages while preserving throughput and cost control.'

[08:00] Tom: Quick meta: how do we coach AEs to pick which demo? The checklist should map buyer signals to demo template — e.g., mention of "latency" -> run the latency demo; mention of "compliance" -> show Private and KMS flows; mention of "unit cost" -> show token-level costing and Optimize suggestions.

[08:20] Miguel: I'll draft a 1-column mapping table.

[08:28] Hannah: Also, short clips. Evan — you said you'd record two 90–180 second micropitch videos that AEs can send. Those should be captioned and include the one-liners.

[08:38] Evan: Yup will do.

[08:42] (brief pause)

[08:48] Mark: Ok before we close, any other objections we need rapid replies for? I still get 'we host our own models' a lot.

[08:55] Priya: For that: 'If you're self-hosting, Redwood can standardize serving across teams — we can reduce duplication and provide shared telemetry and rollout controls — think of it like an ops layer on top of models.'

[09:12] Evan: Good. Let's capture the micro rebuttals in the playbook.

[09:20] (wrap-up starts)

[09:25] Evan: Quick recap and next steps: Priya will update the three demo templates and the checklist; Hannah will write four competitive blurbs for the objection doc; I'll record the micropitch videos; Lena will schedule the roleplay session and invite AEs. We'll aim to reconvene week of 2025-10-13 for roleplay.

[09:46] Lena: I'll book the session and ping calendar.

[09:50] Tom: Cool, thanks everyone.

[09:55] Evan: Thanks all — end of session.

Notes: Transcript includes some imperfect auto-captioning (e.g., 'KV' sometimes 'K-V', 'trace' sometimes 'trayce' etc), filler words retained.
